page_title: Dynamic Application Security Testing with ZAP and GitHub Actions

sources.entry: 1. Dynamic Application Security Testing with ZAP and GitHub Actions

summary.title: Dynamic Application Security Testing with ZAP and GitHub Actions
summary.one_liner: You learn how to run the ZAP full scan GitHub Action to actively test a web application for vulnerabilities on a schedule, with results tracked as GitHub issues.
keywords: how to automate dast in github
takeaways: ZAP full scan runs the spider, an optional ajax spider, and an active scan, so it attacks the target and finds more than the passive baseline scan.
Alerts are reported as a GitHub issue that is updated on new or resolved alerts and closed when all are resolved.
A full scan sends real attack traffic and submits forms, so only test targets you have permission to test and check with your host or CDN first.
A workflow file in .github/workflows (for example zap_scan.yaml) with a cron schedule and the zaproxy full scan action configured with a target URL sets up the scan.
HTML and Markdown reports are attached to each workflow run; a rules file can suppress false positives.
summary.summary: This 2020 ZAP blog post introduces the ZAP full scan GitHub Action for dynamic application security testing (DAST). It explains how the action runs the ZAP spider, an optional ajax spider, and a full active scan against a target, and contrasts this with the passive baseline scan. It covers how results are reported as a GitHub issue that is updated or closed over time, plus HTML and Markdown reports attached to workflow runs. The page includes a sample scheduled YAML workflow that scans a public website, with a warning about running active attacks only on authorized targets. The page is flagged as possibly outdated.
